A recent change on June 2, 2026 I'm aware that has changed recently was [an update to yt-dlp 2026.03.17](https://feedback.vrchat.com/bug-reports/p/yt-dlp-20260303-youtube-1080p-web-web-safari-formats-unavailable-the-page-needs) to fix YouTube `web_safari` extraction and n/sig solving - previously solving n/sig would be skipped and fallback to `android_vr` which doesn't require any JavaScript runtime to extract.

It seems like VRChat is now on yt-dlp `2026.06.09`, which was released two weeks ago on GitHub from this comment. Nothing from the [yt-dlp 2026.06.09 changelogs](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/tag/2026.06.09) stands out for me immediately.

```

PS C:\Users\linda.LINDALAP\AppData\LocalLow\VRChat\VRChat\Tools> .\yt-dlp --version

2026.06.09

```

Regardless of the fans, the CPU @{67968c5b0ab714b24d4b770b|full_name} is using were designed to operate with temperatures up to 95°C.

Not reproducible on Intel Core Ultra 265K with RTX 5080 using yt-dlp `2026.06.09´ from VRChat, even with ` --disable-hw-video-decoding`. yt-dlp on YouTube URLs with `web_safari` formats doesn't place that much of a load with n/sig challenge solving either.

@{67968c5b0ab714b24d4b770b|full_name} should do/share more troubleshooting steps first, including repasting the thermal paste of the CPU, test with various yt-dlp versions against different URLs (both URLs from YouTube using Deno runtime with `web_safari` formats and non-Deno URLs such as direct `.mp4` files on a server), and use HW decoding for video playback if applicable.

details:
I own a PC with a RTX 5080 and a amd ryzen 7 9800x3d and 32GB of ram. My temps are usually around 50°C (rarely 60) in both my CPU and GPU but for the past 2 weeks my CPU been reaching 70°C every time a video stops playing in many worlds. The fans fire up like crazy and that is worrying me. Whenever a video starts the temperatures go back down by 20°C. 

Does anyone got this bug as well? I wanna listen to music and chill with friends but my mind keeps going back to this.
title: AMD CPU firing up with video players
